overview.headline: Newton laws link inertia, force and reaction in flight

keyPoints.point: An object in motion keeps constant speed in a straight line unless an unbalanced force acts
keyPoints.quote: an object in motion remains in motion at constant speed and in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced force.

keyPoints.point: Acceleration depends on mass and the amount of force applied to an object
keyPoints.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

keyPoints.point: If one object exerts a force, the other object exerts an equal and opposite force
keyPoints.quote: If object A exerts a force on object B, object B also exerts an equal and opposite force on object A.

keyPoints.point: This relation holds only for objects that have a constant mass
keyPoints.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.

keyTerms.gloss: tendency to resist changes in motion state
keyTerms.quote: This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.
